qt: to the Commission Mariusz Kamiński (ECR) Subject:

The Telegraph1 draws attention to the dangerous practice of Russian nationals buying up properties in EU Member States located close to sites that are vital to national security. The newspaper points out that Russia is using these properties for operations against Europe as part of its intelligence warfare. An investigation by The Telegraph reveals a network of properties linked to Russians or figures close to the Kremlin that have been purchased near strategic military installations and infrastructure in NATO countries across the Baltic region, specifically Sweden, Lithuania and Norway. The most serious case concerns Sweden2, although similar transactions have been recorded in Lithuania and Latvia. The authors warn of systemic threats. These sites can be used to conduct reconnaissance of military installations, carry out signal interception and surveillance, prepare sabotage and covert operations, stockpile weapons and explosives, and identify targets for future attacks. In light of the aforementioned property acquisitions in locations vital to EU countries: 1.

Is the Commission monitoring the threats posed by Russian nationals buying properties in Member States close to military installations that are critical to EU security, and what is the scale of this activity?
What action does it plan to take to counter the threats outlined above involving the acquisition of properties for use in hostile operations against EU Member States?
Has the Commission taken – or does it intend to take – any steps to block Russian nationals from purchasing property in the EU?
